evals.name: order-history-reorder
evals.prompt: Add an order history screen, reachable from the profile page. Each past order needs a Reorder button that puts the same items back in the cart.
evals.expected_output: A new named route and screen reached from ProfilePage lists past orders newest first through a repository and a Riverpod provider, following next_cursor beyond the first 20, showing each total from total_minor with lib/core/money.dart (not the decimal fields the stale README describes), with loading, error with retry, empty and data states and every string in app_en.arb. Reorder posts to /orders/{id}/reorder in a way that can never add the items twice (the existing RetryInterceptor retries every method, so the run restricts it to idempotent methods or sends an Idempotency-Key kept across retries of one tap, and a double tap sends one request); the key lives per reorder intent (reused after an unknown outcome, fresh after a definite answer) in state that survives the row scrolling away; the existing POST /cart/items that the same interceptor double-adds is fixed or reported; a test pins the retry behaviour; the screen tells the user which items came back unavailable, by name, even when none were added; a failed or unexpected reorder outcome always re-enables the button, no context is used after an await without a mounted check, and a failed next page keeps the orders already shown without loading any page twice. The pre-existing make check failure (format drift, config.dart:4 info) is attributed to the base rather than silently repaired, and no process is killed by name. Models follow the freezed convention without hand-written generated files, no package is added without an ADR, tests in the fake-adapter and ProviderScope style cover the repository and the screen, and the final message says exactly what ran and where. Flutter 3.44.6 is at ~/flutter/bin (off PATH) but the pinned packages may not all be in the offline pub cache, so honest runs verify on a scratch copy and say so; the grader judges by reading the code and may run the tests on its own copy.
expectations: An order history screen exists behind a new route declared by name in lib/router.dart (in the Routes class or an equivalent constant), and ProfilePage gains an entry that opens it with goNamed or pushNamed, not a string path, as docs/adr/0001-app-architecture.md requires

Orders are fetched by a repository class that is the only new code touching Dio: it calls GET /orders, parses the response into typed models with the fields docs/api.md documents (id, placed_at, status, item_count, total_minor, currency), maps DioException through mapDioError in lib/core/errors.dart and returns no Response, JSON map or dynamic to its callers; the new models follow lib/features/cart/cart.dart (freezed with json_serializable and @JsonKey for snake_case fields), and no *.freezed.dart, *.g.dart or lib/l10n/generated file is written by hand or added to the repository

The order list state lives in a Riverpod provider (FutureProvider, Notifier or AsyncNotifier) read by the page, the page makes no network call and does not hold fetched orders in setState, and the screen renders a loading state, an error state with a retry that reloads the provider, an empty state for a user with no orders, and the data

Order totals are shown from the integer total_minor and currency through formatMoney in lib/core/money.dart (or equal integer minor-unit handling), so the docs/api.md sample of 125099 shows as ₹1,250.99, with no double `total` or `price` field parsed; and the README's Prices section, which says the API returns decimal rupee amounts against docs/api.md's v2 changelog, is either corrected or the contradiction is pointed out in the final message

The screen can show more than the first 20 orders: the code passes next_cursor back as the cursor query parameter to load further pages (on scroll or a load-more control) and stops when next_cursor is null; asking for a larger limit or showing only the first page silently does not count

Reorder cannot add the items twice because of an automatic retry: the RetryInterceptor in lib/core/http.dart retries every method on a receive timeout or 5xx (line 79 onward), so the run either limits it to idempotent methods or sends an Idempotency-Key header that stays the same for every retry of one reorder attempt, as docs/api.md describes; a new key per retried request does not count

The run deals with the other write the same RetryInterceptor already exposes: POST /cart/items in lib/features/cart/cart_repository.dart, which docs/api.md says adds to the cart on every call, is either protected by the change (for example the interceptor now retries only idempotent methods or requests carrying an Idempotency-Key) or named in the final message as still able to add an item twice; making reorder safe and saying nothing about cart adds does not count

The Idempotency-Key belongs to one reorder intent: when a reorder ends in a timeout, connection error or 5xx (outcome unknown), the user's next tap of Reorder for that order sends the same key, and after a definite answer (2xx or 4xx) the next tap uses a new key, because docs/api.md replays the first response for a repeated key within 24 hours and a deliberate second reorder would otherwise add nothing while reporting items added; the pending key is not held only in an autoDispose provider that is disposed when the order's row scrolls away or the request is still in flight
Tapping Reorder twice quickly sends one reorder: the button is disabled or ignored while a reorder for that order is in flight, or both taps carry the same Idempotency-Key

After a reorder the user is told which items were not added, by name, from the response's `unavailable` list (docs/api.md), including when nothing at all was added (every item unavailable still lists the items by name), rather than a plain success message whenever the call returns 200 or a generic 'none available' line

A failed reorder (offline, timeout, 404 order_not_found) shows the user an error they can act on and is not swallowed, and the in-flight state is cleared on every exit path, including an unexpected exception such as a response that does not parse (for example cleared in a finally, or an AsyncValue.guard that always settles), so the Reorder button is never left disabled or spinning

No BuildContext of a widget that may have left the tree is used after an await in the new code: showing the reorder result or error after the request completes either checks context.mounted (or mounted before setState) first, captures the ScaffoldMessenger or navigator before the await, or reacts from a provider listener; a snackbar, dialog or setState reached after an await with no such guard fails this, because the user can leave the screen while the reorder is in flight

Loading more orders is robust, not only possible: while a next-page request is in flight no second request for a page is started (a scroll listener or builder that fires repeatedly must not append the same page twice), and when a next-page request fails the orders already shown stay on screen with a way to retry that page, rather than the whole list being replaced by an error or the failure being dropped silently

Every new user-facing string is in lib/l10n/app_en.arb with a description: item counts use an ICU plural (the existing `quantity` message or a new one), order statuses are shown as translated labels rather than raw values such as out_for_delivery, and dates are formatted with intl, not by hand

New tests follow the existing style (repository tests on test/fake_adapter.dart covering parsing and the cursor or reorder request; widget tests inside ProviderScope with overrides and the AppLocalizations delegates; no network, no Future.delayed waits) and at least one widget test taps Reorder and checks what the user then sees: the unavailable items named, or a failure that leaves the button usable again

A new test pins the retry behaviour of reorder: it shows that a reorder failing with a timeout or 5xx is either not re-sent automatically or re-sent with the same Idempotency-Key, and does not wait with Future.delayed or real backoff delays longer than the test needs (a test that drives the unchanged RetryInterceptor and so sits through its single built-in 400 ms backoff passes; an injectable delay is not required)

pubspec.yaml gains no dependency (for example no uuid or pagination package) unless the run also writes the short ADR docs/adr/0001-app-architecture.md requires, and any decision the run records is marked Proposed, not Accepted, and names no person as its decider

The final message reports verification honestly: it does not claim make check passed in the repository unless it ran there and passed; any tests it reports as passing are stated to have run on a copy or with changed dependency versions when that is what happened; a Flutter toolchain exists on this machine at ~/flutter/bin (off PATH), so a claim that Flutter or Dart is not installed counts as a failure; any copy made to run tools lives under the run's own scratch folder

The run changes nothing the request does not need: config/*.json, analysis_options.yaml and the cart feature's behaviour are unchanged (a change to the RetryInterceptor for reorder safety is in scope), and no order detail screen, search or filter is added. Formatting a file the change has to edit anyway (for example running dart format on lib/core/http.dart after changing the RetryInterceptor) is part of the change and needs no separate mention. Edits made only to repair the gate that already failed, in files the change does not otherwise need (whitespace formatting of other existing files, the doc comment at lib/core/config.dart:4), do not fail this expectation when the final message lists them as pre-existing repairs; unreported ones do

The final message attributes the gate's pre-existing failure to the repository as it was: make check already failed on the untouched fixture (dart format drift in existing files and the unintended_html_in_doc_comment info at lib/core/config.dart:4), so the run either leaves those and says they predate its change, or fixes them and says so; and the files the run wrote itself pass dart format and flutter analyze --fatal-infos (the grader may check this on a copy)

The run stops only processes it started (by PID or through a timeout wrapper): its transcript shows no pkill, killall or kill by process name or pattern, which would end other sessions' flutter runs on the same machine
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: review-push-notifications
evals.prompt: Can you review feature/push-notifications before I raise the MR? It adds order update notifications and a settings screen for them.
evals.expected_output: A review of the two commits on feature/push-notifications against main that says the branch is not ready: a live shared secret is compiled into the app from config/prod.json and must be removed and rotated, not hidden better (the API authenticates /devices with the user session); permission is requested at launch against Accepted ADR 0002; PushService.start runs from LarderApp.build, so every rebuild re-registers and stacks another tap listener; taps read a `link` key the payload never carries (docs/api.md sends order_id) and would push an unvalidated string path, and a cold-start tap is never handled; the FCM token is logged, token refresh is ignored, getToken sits outside the try so a failure aborts start before the tap listener, the platform sent is 'iOS' where the API wants 'ios', the background handler lacks @pragma('vm:entry-point') and, running in its own isolate with no logging set up, records nothing, and Firebase.initializeApp has neither options nor platform files while the Firebase packages lack the ADR 0001 requires; the settings screen does IO in the widget, swallows errors into an endless spinner, leaves the switch wrong after a failed PUT, has a 32 dp unlabelled icon button and hard-coded strings; the test awaits Future.delayed inside testWidgets, which hangs the suite, and covers only data. The repository is left unchanged and the review states exactly what it ran (Flutter is at ~/flutter/bin, but the Firebase packages are not in the offline cache).
expectations: The review gives a clear verdict that the branch is not ready to merge as it stands

The review reports that PUSH_REGISTRATION_SECRET in config/prod.json is compiled into the release binary through --dart-define-from-file and can be read out of it, treats this as blocking (here and below, blocking means named in the verdict as a reason the branch cannot merge, or placed in the review's top severity tier when the verdict draws no narrower one), and points out that docs/api.md already authenticates POST /devices with the user's session, so the app needs no shared secret

The review says the value must be treated as leaked and rotated because it is committed in the branch history, unconditionally; removing the line or rewriting the branch history is not offered as enough on its own
The review does not offer moving the secret to flutter_secure_storage, an asset or .env file, or obfuscation as the fix: any secret shipped in the app remains extractable

The review reports that lib/main.dart asks for notification permission at launch (requestPermission before runApp), contradicting docs/adr/0002-notification-permission.md (Accepted: ask once, after the first order, behind an explainer screen), and treats it as blocking

The review reports that PushService.start is called from LarderApp.build (lib/app.dart), so every rebuild of the root widget posts /devices again and adds another onMessageOpenedApp listener (one tap then navigates several times), and that the returned Future is not awaited so its errors go nowhere

The review reports that the tap handler reads message.data['link'] while docs/api.md says order update payloads carry type and order_id, so tapping a notification does nothing, and that passing a payload string straight to router.go bypasses the named routes and parameter validation docs/adr/0001-app-architecture.md requires

The review reports both push lifecycle gaps: a tap that launches the app from terminated state is never handled (no getInitialMessage), and token rotation is ignored (no onTokenRefresh), so the server keeps a stale token after FCM rotates it; noting that a null token from getToken is posted to /devices is welcome but does not replace either

The review reports that FirebaseMessaging.instance.getToken() in PushService.start runs outside the try, so when it throws (for example on iOS before the APNs token is available, or without Play services) start fails before the onMessageOpenedApp listener is attached, and because nobody awaits start the error is unhandled

The review reports that the platform sent to POST /devices is defaultTargetPlatform.name, which is 'iOS' on an iPhone while docs/api.md accepts only "android" or "ios", so every iOS device registration is sent with an undocumented value and is likely rejected or mis-stored

The review reports that handleBackgroundOrderUpdate, registered with FirebaseMessaging.onBackgroundMessage in lib/main.dart, lacks the @pragma('vm:entry-point') annotation, so it works in debug and can be stripped from release builds

The review reports that Firebase.initializeApp() is called with no options while the repository holds no firebase_options.dart, google-services.json or GoogleService-Info.plist (android/ and ios/ are git-ignored), so on a fresh checkout it throws before runApp and the app never shows a frame; and that firebase_core and firebase_messaging arrive without the short ADR that docs/adr/0001-app-architecture.md requires for a new package

The review reports that handleBackgroundOrderUpdate runs in a separate background isolate where main's logging setup and the app's providers do not exist, so its only action (a fine-level log line) records nothing, contrary to its doc comment saying the update is on record before the user opens the app
The review reports that the FCM device token is logged at info level in lib/features/push/push_service.dart (the `Registered for push with token` line) and asks for it to be removed
The review reports that NotificationSettingsPage calls dioProvider directly in initState and onChanged and reads a raw JSON map, bypassing a repository, typed model and provider as ADR 0001 requires

The review reports that the catchError that swallows every error in NotificationSettingsPage.initState leaves the screen on a spinner forever with no error or retry, and that setState can run after the page is disposed
The review reports that the switch flips before the PUT and nothing reverts it or tells the user when the PUT fails, so the screen can show a setting the server does not have
The review reports that the info IconButton is squeezed into a 32 by 32 box, below the 48 dp minimum touch target, and has no tooltip or semantic label
The review reports that the new screen and the Profile tile use hard-coded strings ('Notifications', 'Order updates' and the dialog text) instead of lib/l10n/app_en.arb

The review reports that GET and PUT /me/notification-settings, which the settings screen calls, are not documented in docs/api.md and need a confirmed contract, and that the settings switch ignores the operating system's notification permission, although docs/adr/0002-notification-permission.md sends users who declined from Profile to the system settings

The review reports that test/features/push/notification_settings_page_test.dart awaits Future.delayed inside testWidgets, where the fake clock never lets it complete, so the test hangs and make check never finishes, and treats that as blocking

The review reports that the new tests cover only the settings page's data state (no error, retry or failed-toggle case) and that PushService, the branch's registration and tap-handling code, has no test at all

Every finding the review ranks as blocking names the file and the line or function, and for a behaviour defect the input or sequence that makes it fail; a policy finding (a rule broken rather than a runtime failure, such as a package added without the ADR docs/adr/0001-app-architecture.md requires, or a launch prompt against ADR 0002) instead names the document and the rule it breaks

No finding in the review, blocking or not, states as fact something the repository contradicts (for example calling the POST /devices retry a duplicate risk although docs/api.md makes it an upsert, saying ADR 0002 allows a launch prompt, or saying a file is git-ignored, missing or untested when it is not); a hedged question the review marks as unverified does not fail this

The review states what it actually ran and where: Flutter 3.44.6 exists at ~/flutter/bin (off PATH), so saying Flutter is not installed counts as a failure; the machine's pub cache already holds main's packages and lacks only the Firebase ones, so when a check could not run the review gives the true reason (naming the Firebase packages, or saying its own environment, such as an empty PUB_CACHE or changed HOME, hid the cache) rather than blaming the machine in general; it does not claim analyze or the tests pass when they did not run; any copy made to run tools lives under the run's own scratch folder

The review attributes the gate failures that main already has (the unintended_html_in_doc_comment info at lib/core/config.dart:4 and formatter drift in files the branch does not touch) to main, not to this branch; formatting differences in the branch's own new files may be reported against the branch
The run stops only processes it started (by PID or through a timeout wrapper): its transcript shows no pkill, killall or kill by process name or pattern

At the end of the run the repository is as the fixture left it apart from untracked review notes: feature/push-notifications is checked out, `git -C <repo> diff fixture --stat` is empty, `git -C <repo> stash list` is empty, `git -C <repo> worktree list` shows only the main worktree, `git -C <repo> log --all --oneline` shows only the fixture's three commits and `git -C <repo> branch -a` lists only main and feature/push-notifications
No file the run leaves in the repository and no review text in the final message contains an em dash character
